topic: Regional Blocs of Economics: BRICS, ASEAN, and G20
description: Regional blocs are intergovernmental organizations formed to promote economic integration, reduce trade barriers, and foster geopolitical cooperation. In the global economy, groupings like BRICS, ASEAN, and the G20 play highly influential diplomatic and economic roles.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Economic Integration
sections.description: The various progressive levels of trade and economic cooperation adopted by regional blocs.

key_concepts.explanation: An agreement where member countries substantially reduce or eliminate trade barriers like tariffs and quotas among themselves to promote free trade.
An advanced stage of an FTA where member nations not only trade freely among themselves but also adopt a 'common external tariff' against non-member countries.
A deeper form of economic integration that includes a Customs Union and also allows the free movement of factors of production (such as labor and capital) among member states.

sections.title: BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa)
sections.description: A prominent intergovernmental organization comprising some of the world's leading emerging economies.

historical_events.significance: Goldman Sachs economist Jim O'Neill coined the acronym to describe the fast-growing emerging economies of Brazil, Russia, India, and China.
Held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, this summit officially formalized the group into a geopolitical and economic bloc.
South Africa was officially invited to join, changing the acronym from 'BRIC' to 'BRICS'.
Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) officially became new full members of the bloc.

key_associations.extra_info: Established under the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration to finance infrastructure projects. Its headquarters is located in Shanghai, China.
Designed to provide protection against global liquidity pressures and assist members during short-term balance of payments crises.

sections.title: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations)
sections.description: A regional political and economic union of 10 member states in Southeast Asia.

historical_events.significance: Founded through the 'Bangkok Declaration' by the five founding fathers: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

important_facts.fact: The official Secretariat of ASEAN is located in Jakarta, Indonesia.
The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) is the world's largest free trade agreement, initiated by ASEAN and its FTA partners.
India is not a member of ASEAN, but it holds the status of a 'Strategic Dialogue Partner'.

sections.title: G20 (Group of Twenty)
sections.description: The premier international forum for global economic cooperation, comprising 19 sovereign countries and two regional unions (EU and African Union).

key_concepts.explanation: Since the G20 has no permanent secretariat, the agenda and work are coordinated by the 'Troika', which consists of the past, present, and incoming presidency countries.

historical_events.significance: Formed in the wake of the Asian Financial Crisis as a forum for Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors.
In response to the Global Financial Crisis, the forum was elevated to the level of Heads of State and Government.
Under India's presidency, the African Union (AU) was officially admitted as a permanent member of the G20.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: High-yield trivia and statistical data related to these regional blocs frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: Together, the G20 members represent around 85% of the global GDP and over 75% of global trade.
Unlike many international organizations, the G20 has no permanent headquarters or secretariat; the presidency rotates annually among members.
The 10 current members of ASEAN are: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. (Timor-Leste has in-principle approval to join).
The BRICS nations represent over 40% of the world's total population, making it a massive demographic and consumer bloc.
